reference: GNU lsof is used only for a safe missing-option-argument exit-status comparison. Help and version cases assert documented Bash builtin contracts; live /proc queries are deferred.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata
missing -p and -u arguments and rejection of a nonnumeric operand
GNU lsof comparison of missing -p argument status
deferred controlled PID, user-filter, and process-table queries
exclusions: No lsof case enumerates or reads /proc during validation.
PID descriptor listing, user filtering, and whole-table enumeration require a disposable VM or an independently reviewed procfs mock with controlled processes.

cases.purpose: Check that Bash reports lsof as a builtin and that help exposes the documented description and synopsis.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t lsof)
[[ $kind == builtin ]]
help lsof >metadata.help
have_description=0
have_synopsis=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  case $line in
    *'List open file descriptors via /proc/PID/fd.'*) have_description=1 ;;
    *'lsof [-p PID]... [-u USER] [PID...]'*) have_synopsis=1 ;;
  esac
done <metadata.help
[[ $have_description == 1 && $have_synopsis == 1 ]]
printf 'builtin-metadata-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Qualify -p listing of known open descriptor types and paths against GNU lsof.
cases.reason: Never executed. An ordinary owned child is enough: each side starts its own fixed-name helper holding known descriptors, and the side verifies the PID it queried is that child.

cases.purpose: Qualify -u name and numeric-UID filtering across processes with distinct owners.
cases.reason: Never executed. Two distinct owners are already visible in the guest (root controller and uid 2000), and the VM passwd provides names, so no capability is missing.

cases.purpose: Qualify default whole-table enumeration and filtering over a deterministic process set.
cases.reason: Never executed. A deterministic set is reachable unprivileged with a nested 'unshare -Urpf --mount-proc' (util-linux, absolute path), so only the fixture's own processes are visible. This assumes unprivileged user namespaces are enabled in the guest kernel (check user.max_user_namespaces in the VM).
